title: The Cycle of the Judges
hint: The recurring pattern in the time of the Judges
intro: Judges chapter 2 introduces the tragic pattern that repeats throughout the book: sin → punishment → cry for help → deliverance → peace → new sin. This cycle repeated itself in seven rounds over about 350 years.

items.title: The People Forsake the Lord
items.text: After Joshua's death, the Israelites abandoned the Lord, the God of their ancestors, and worshiped Baal and Ashtoreth—the gods of the peoples around them.

items.title: The Lord's Anger
items.text: The Lord's anger burned against Israel. He handed them over to raiders and sold them into the hands of their enemies around them.

items.title: The People Cry Out
items.text: When their distress became too great, the people cried out to the Lord for help.

items.title: The Lord Raises Up a Judge
items.text: The Lord raised up judges who delivered them from the hands of their raiders. The Lord was with the judge and saved them as long as the judge lived.

items.title: Peace in the Land
items.text: As long as the judge lived, the people had peace from their enemies.

items.title: The Cycle Repeats
items.text: But when the judge died, the people turned back and acted even more wickedly than their ancestors. They followed other gods, served them and worshiped them. They did not give up their evil ways.

footer.title: The Twelve Judges
footer.content: The book describes twelve judges: Othniel, Ehud, Shamgar, Deborah, Gideon, Tola, Jair, Jephthah, Ibzan, Elon, Abdon and Samson. The cycle shows humanity's tendency to forget God in good times—and God's faithful grace when we turn back.
